issues.description: Unbounded in-memory log buffer with no cap or eviction policy
issues.detail: _BufferingHandler appends every LogRecord to self.buffer with no size limit, no time bound, and no eviction. The invariant 'buffer holds records until session.start() flushes them' silently breaks when session.start() is delayed or never reached: the handler keeps growing for the entire job lifetime. On a wedged job that never crashes and never calls init_recording, this leaks memory monotonically. A literate version would state the bound (e.g., 'at most N records or M bytes, FIFO-evicted') and enforce it in emit(). collections.deque(maxlen=N) is the right data structure here, not list.

issues.description: O(n*m) handler scan on every flush and shutdown without justification
issues.detail: _flush_early_log_buffer iterates logging.getLogger().handlers looking for the first LoggingHandler, and _shutdown_telemetry does the same. Each call is O(handlers) and silently assumes exactly one OTLP LoggingHandler is the right target. The invariant being relied on ('the OTLP handler installed by _setup_cloud_tracer is unique and identifiable by isinstance(LoggingHandler)') is never stated and not robust: any other library that adds an opentelemetry LoggingHandler will be matched first. Either capture the handler reference at install time (correct data-structure choice: a direct pointer, not a linear search over a global) or document the invariant in a literate comment.

issues.description: Replay path bypasses the log filter that decorates records with job context
issues.detail: _on_setup installs self._log_filter on existing handlers via addFilter so records get job/session attribution. The new _BufferingHandler is added to the root logger without that filter, and on replay the buffered records are pushed directly into the OTLP LoggingHandler via h.emit(record). Records captured before init_recording therefore lack whatever attributes the filter normally injects, and the OTLP-side filter on the LoggingHandler is also bypassed because emit() is called directly rather than going through Logger.handle(). The invariant 'every uploaded log record has been filtered' silently breaks for exactly the crash logs you most want to attribute.

issues.description: Reverting pytest -n auto and dropping a test file with no stated reason
issues.detail: The makefile change removes parallel test execution (-n auto) and drops tests/test_plugin_google_stt.py from the unit-tests target. Neither change is mentioned in the PR description and neither is commented in the diff. From a literate-code standpoint these are exactly the kind of edits a reader cannot reconstruct without git archaeology: 'why is this slower now? why is this test gone?' Either restore them or leave a one-line comment in the makefile explaining the constraint (flaky under xdist, plugin test moved, etc.).

issues.description: Set-result race between _on_entry_done and a concurrent shutdown is suppressed, not reasoned about
issues.detail: The new _on_entry_done forces self._shutdown_fut.set_result(...) under contextlib.suppress(asyncio.InvalidStateError). This is fine operationally, but the invariant being asserted is 'whichever setter wins, the eventual reason is acceptable.' That isn't obvious: if user-initiated shutdown wins, the crash reason is lost; if the crash setter wins, an in-flight user shutdown sees user_initiated=False. A one-line comment naming this ordering and confirming the downstream cleanup is reason-agnostic would make the code readable without running it.

issues.description: _flush_early_log_buffer silently no-ops if no OTLP LoggingHandler is found
issues.detail: If the loop over root handlers finds no LoggingHandler, the buffered records are dropped on the floor without a warning. For the crash-log path specifically (init_recording called from _on_cleanup after a failure), this is the failure mode the PR is trying to fix; a silent miss here defeats the purpose. A logger.warning('OTLP handler not present; %d buffered records dropped', len(handler.buffer)) would make the failure observable.

issues.description: Test assertion weakened from 'retry succeeds' to 'retry also times out' without a stated invariant
issues.detail: tests/test_ipc.py previously asserted 'after initialization failure, warmup should be retried' and waited for start_q only. The new version waits for both start_q and close_q, with the comment 'retry batch should also timeout and be killed.' This is a meaningful behavioral change in what the pool is asserted to do (does it retry indefinitely? does it back off? is the second batch expected to also fail?). The comment states the new observed behavior but not the invariant being protected. A reader cannot tell whether this test now passes because of the fix or because of an unrelated change in retry semantics.

issues.description: Lazy import of RecordingOptions inside _on_cleanup hides a module-load-order assumption
issues.detail: _on_cleanup does 'from .voice.agent_session import RecordingOptions' inline and wraps init_recording in a bare except. The inline import is defensive against circular imports, but that constraint isn't stated. A two-line literate comment ('imported lazily to avoid a job <-> voice.agent_session cycle; failures here must not mask the original crash, hence broad except') would make this readable without spelunking the import graph.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED with one NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT and one WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE finding. The core mechanism — buffer early, replay on init, force shutdown_fut on crash — is sound and addresses a real observability gap. But the buffer is an unbounded list where it should be a bounded deque, the OTLP handler is rediscovered by linear isinstance scan in two places where a captured reference would be both faster and more correct, and the replay path bypasses the _log_filter that normally attributes records to the job. The makefile changes (dropping -n auto and a test file) and the test assertion flip in test_ipc.py are undocumented behavioral edits a careful reader cannot reconstruct from the diff. Tighten the buffer's invariant, state the handler-uniqueness assumption (or capture the reference), and add one-line literate comments to the makefile and test changes before merging.
